failure_model: The planned changed-path classifier correctly reuses the *new* manifest's recursive-glob vocabulary.
If one commit edits V030_RELEASE_LOCK.json and removes its own `docs/V030_RELEASE_LOCK.json` fingerprint entry, that changed manifest path can become invisible to the new vocabulary.
Without a structural self-anchor, an authority-surface mutation can therefore redefine the matcher that decides whether that same mutation invalidates evidence.
new_finding.why_distinct: This is separate from the open fnmatch P1. Unifying matcher semantics does not by itself prevent the manifest from deleting its own admission anchor.

cheapest_repair.invariant: Canonical load_manifest() must fail closed unless `docs/V030_RELEASE_LOCK.json` remains in fingerprint_globs.
cheapest_repair.classifier_behavior: authoritative-v2 must load the manifest through that validator; a malformed/self-unanchored manifest makes classifier red rather than stale-green.
cheapest_repair.regression: Remove only the self fingerprint entry from an otherwise valid manifest and assert canonical load rejects it.
cheapest_repair.scope: Do not hard-code the entire mutable 85-pattern surface. Only ratchet the authority document's self-anchor; ordinary surface evolution remains permitted and fingerprint-changing.

relation_to_three_layer_repair: Layer 1: authoritative-v2 cheap classifier must wake broadly enough to observe manifest changes.
Layer 2: cumulative merge-base PR candidate scope must carry the manifest mutation.
Layer 2b: canonical matcher must be self-anchored so the changed manifest cannot make itself irrelevant.
Layer 3: exact-SHA substantive receipts remain required; classifier-only green never satisfies authority.
